newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-SCHALKE AND TENERIFE EYE FIRST EUROPEAN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCHALKE AND TENERIFE EYE FIRST EUROPEAN FINAL.

text.p: Schalke will attempt to forget their recent poor league form when they take on Tenerife on Tuesday with a place in the UEFA Cup final at stake.
The Gelsenkirchen side are without a win in their last six games and their immediate priority is to pull back the 1-0 lead Tenerife established in the Canary Islands in the first leg two weeks ago.
But libero Olaf Thon is convinced Schalke will rise to the occasion and reach a European final for the first time.
"Bundesliga and European competition are two different worlds and I think we'll make it," Thon said.
As they were in Tenerife, Schalke will be without their first-choice strike force of Youri Mulder and Martin Max, who are both injured.

Coach Huub Stevens is also concerned about the freshness of U.S. internationals Tom Dooley and David Wagner, who played for their country against Mexico on Sunday and were only due to arrive back from the game in Foxboro, Massachusetts, on Monday.
Tenerife, coached by German Jupp Heynckes, meanwhile take a slender advantage into the match, but are at a considerable disadvantage after having two players sent off in the first leg.

Argentine goalkeeper Marcello Ojeda and midfielder Angel Vivar Dorado were both sent off in the first leg and will miss the return which, as in Schalke's case, could be the Spanish side's last stepping stone to their first European final.
Swede Beng Andersson, who did well when he came on as a substitute for the dismissed Ojeda in the first leg, will keep his place.
But Tenerife will be hit by the absences of forward Antonio Robaina, midfielder Angel Vivar Dorado and Juan Juanele Castano who are all suspended.
Juanele, the architect of the first-leg victory, will be particularly missed, although he missed a penalty in Saturday's 1-0 home defeat by Real Betis.
The game once again proved that Jupp Heynckes' side are better at creating chances than taking them.
Heynckes used several substitutes in the game and has no injury problems apart from the long-standing one to Czech midfielder Pavel Hapel.
Heynckes, who has been linked with several German teams, said he is happy in Spain, although his differences with the Tenerife board are well known.
"I will continue in Spain, that's for sure. I want to stay here, as both I and my family have acclimatised very well."
Schalke: Jens Lehmann; Olaf Thon, Johan de Kock, Thomas Linke, Yves Eigenrauch, Jiri Nemec; Andreas Mueller, Ingo Anderbruegge, Mike Bueskens; Radoslav Latal, Marc Wilmots.
Tenerife: Beng Andersson; Alexis Suarez, Cesar Gomez, Sergio Ballesteros, Antonio Mata, Chano Cruzado; Dani Gonzalez, Felipe Minambres, Slavisa Jokanovic; Meho Kodro, Antonio Pinilla.
